interactions.title: Recap: Inakara’s passage and the clan shield
lines: DM: You, earlier this afternoon, like five sessions ago, you left your horses and gear in the narrow river valley and made your way by secret passages and wading rivers through the mountains to the abandoned dwarven outpost near that Dunmari stronghold of Raven's Hold. There, after encountering Inakara and her wild unidentified kin and obtaining safe passage in exchange for some combat, you found your way to the Brawnanvil vault, where Riswynn recovered her long-sought heirloom shield of her clan, enchanted to preserve the stories of her—her family's history.

before: Seeker: Cool.
Unknown: And...
DM: OK, so we begin tonight as the sun is setting over Raven's Hold.
after: DM: Leaving the dwarven stronghold via an underground passage, seemingly constructed after the dwarves had abandoned their outpost, as neither Riswynn nor her uncle who drew the map had any indication that existed. Or, sorry. You found yourself emerging in a series of storerooms carved into a cliff wall. One of which seemed to have been used as a prison or torture chamber, execution chamber, by hobgoblins, presumably, at some point, but after the Dunmari had built the stronghold, when they had captured it and occupied it, perhaps during their wars with the Dunmari in the Blood Years.

DM: After defeating some seemingly recently reanimated undead hobgoblin corpses, some careful scouting revealed signs of gnoll occupation, along with a large number of wild beasts being kept for some unknown purpose. You then found an unguarded passage to the two guard towers of the inner keep, where, in one of these towers, you encountered and freed a prisoner, Vola. Vola Forena of Chardon, who is being guarded by an orc and two shapeshifting jackalweres, seemingly the servants of some entity that she referred to as Agata Dustmother.

DM: Now it's dusk. Red light of the sunset is streaming through the narrow windows of the north tower, where you have come to catch your breath in what seems to be the ruined and decaying remains of a study or council chamber of some kind. Outside, you can hear the howls of beasts—hyenas, lions, jackals, wild dogs—in the distance, fading and then growing stronger as something stirs them up, and then fading again, from the outer courtyard beyond the towers. The stench of rotting sulphurous flesh and a faint tinge of ash in your mouth rises from the inner courtyard on the other side. A flicker of firelight gleams from the windows and the open door of the main keep.

DM: As you kind of come in, bar the door, begin to clear some space to sit and catch your breath, Vola turns to you and says, "I could really use a real meal, to be honest. It's not like those bloody creatures fed me much. And then perhaps we can make a plan to get the fuck out of this damn place. Do you think you have some food?"
Delwath: Sure, some rations.
